stem: In the inequality \(3x + k \le 2x + 10\), \(k\) is a constant. Every value of \(x\) with \(x \le 6\) is a solution to the inequality. What is the greatest possible value of \(k\)?
solution: Subtract \(2x\) and \(k\) from both sides: \(x \le 10 - k\).
Every \(x \le 6\) must satisfy \(x \le 10 - k\). This is true exactly when \(6 \le 10 - k\).
So \(k \le 4\), and the greatest possible value of \(k\) is 4.
verify:
x = symbols('x')
works = lambda kv: Interval(-oo, 6).is_subset(solve_univariate_inequality(3*x + kv <= 2*x + 10, x, relational=False))
assert works(4) and not works(Rational(401, 100))
assert [Rational(a) for a in spr_answers] == [4]
